newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Central Bank defies rumours of rupiah band change.
newsitem.headline: Central Bank defies rumours of rupiah band change.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank continued to defy foreign speculation on a widening of the rupiah's intervention band and snapped up dollars to keep the rupiah from rising too high, currency dealers said on Monday.
Offshore currency operators had bought rupiah on Friday, speculating that a widening of the intervention band was imminent. Past widenings of the band had caused the rupiah to appreciate sharply.
Currency dealers said the speculation continued on Monday.
"It's less vigorous than Friday, but enough to maintain upward momentum for the rupiah," one currency dealer said.
At 0850 GMT, spot rupiah fall back slightly to 2364.40/5.40, after opening on Monday at 2,363.75/64.10.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point late on Monday to 2,364/2,556.

The intervention band is an optimal rupiah-dollar exchange range set daily by the bank. If the rupiah rises or falls out of the band, Bank Indonesia intervenes in the foreign exchange market to keep the currency stable.
The band has become the market focus since the central bank widened its band to eight percent from five percent last September.
Currency dealers in Jakarta said the central bank was estimated to have absorbed at least $1.1 billion last Friday to keep the rupiah from rising out of the intervention band.
They said the impact was felt in the market, with swap premiums tumbling across the board on expectation of ample rupiah liquidity on Tuesday induced by central bank dollar-buying.
Swap rates are premiums which allow operators to roll over positions established in the cash market.
One local bank dealer said offshore operators were still challenging the central bank on Monday to widen its band after they failed last Friday.
Central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono shrugged off market speculation last week by saying monetary policy would be kept flexible and adjusted whenever necessary.
However, he also said the rupiah exchange rate would be kept at a realistic level without anti-export bias.
Dealers said there were rumours in the market that the central bank might try to teach speculators a lesson by tightening the allocation of central bank papers (SBIs) this week.
SBIs are central bank instruments used to tighten liquidity in the money market and are also options for offshore investors to park their funds temporarily.
"If the rumours come true, people with ample rupiah might be squeezed if they haven't placed their rupiah yet. Interbank rates this morning have given the signals," the dealer said.
He said he doubted offshore operators had found alternate rupiah investments, which may result in further roll-overs of existing short dollar positions.
"This is a tug-of-war. I don't know how long they can hold. They are now being squeezed on the swap side," he added.
The dealer said some offshore operators appeared to have given up for now, which was reflected in the dollar's slight recovery since Friday.
The dollar dropped three points below the central bank intervention band last Friday on heavy band speculation.
Dealers said offshore operators might be forced to buy back dollars if they started to calculate the value of their speculation.
Dealers said offshore operators were seen mainly sustaining short dollar positions as reflected in declining tom/next swap rates, which were traded below par levels.
"If they can't find adequate rupiah investments and cannot get out of the swap market, they will buy back," another said.
Dealers in Jakarta said offshore operators seemed to be trying to launch another attack on the band by spreading rumours of a band widening on Wednesday.
They said Wednesday was selected as the day because some players usually went short on dollars on Wednesdays and bought them back on Thursdays to enjoy weekend rupiah premiums.
